title: CMOS inverter amplifier
description: A CMOS inverter used as an analog amplifier: the input drives both an NMOS and a PMOS gate, and the two devices share one drain current stacked between the rails (current reuse). Because both transconductances act on the same input, the stage transconductance is the sum gm_tot = n_gm + p_gm, so the inverter gives roughly twice the gm of a single device at the same current - the reason it is the workhorse gain cell for low-voltage, power-efficient design. The gain is gm_tot/(n_gds + p_gds). Both devices are composed children biased at the same current; pick the PMOS child table to the p polarity and set p_sign to -1 for a signed-PMOS axis.

params.name: V_out
params.note: output DC level; sets both devices' drain-source voltages (ideally near mid-supply)

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate (both drains + wiring); refine from extraction

params.name: I_bias
params.note: the single current both devices carry (current reuse)

params.name: gm_id_p
params.note: PMOS inversion; match the two gm/ID for a balanced transfer and lowest offset

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS table: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: NMOS device
doc.description: The pull-down device at the shared current, drain at the output. Exposes its transconductance, output conductance, saturation headroom, current, and channel-noise density.

doc.title: PMOS device
doc.description: The pull-up device at the shared current, drain at the output. Exposes its transconductance, output conductance, saturation headroom, and current.

params.name: vds_d
params.note: source-to-drain headroom, signed to this table's axis convention

rows.name: gm_tot
rows.note: current reuse: both devices' transconductances act on the same input and add

rows.name: gout
rows.note: both output conductances load the node

rows.name: Av
rows.note: combined transconductance into the combined output conductance

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: both channel-noise currents (4kTgamma*gm each) sum and refer to the input by gm_tot, giving sqrt(4kTgamma/gm_tot)
